findings.text: Upheld as advisory (Q10). The comment above the answer restates the code under it and the doc comment above the function (the four keys every answer carries, the three a server step adds); it says what, not why. Q10 is not a defect class of the rubric. The line is an added line of the diff.

Upheld as advisory (Q5). `contextOf` runs on every call, while only the two refusal branches (`statusOf(prepared, context)`, `statusOf(outcome, context)`) read it; the success path pays one read it does not use. A cost, not a dead path or a hidden fallback. The reviewer read one file in full this round; the other files were read in rounds 1 to 3, are unchanged since but for the tests and the docs this cut names, and the test and doc edits are covered by the test-quality, risk and architecture readings below.

Upheld as advisory (public-api, Q6/Q3). A member who learns a lost name's id can re-create it with that id after a restore and the server does not check that this member created it; teammates' `recreated` detection then never fires. It widens nothing, since any member may already push under any held name (ADR 0026 D-11). Carried from rounds 1 to 3 at the same severity; the line is unchanged.

Upheld as advisory (personal-data, Q4). `serve purge name` sets `purged_at` only; the alias and the creator columns stay in `names`, the change, revision and audit rows, and the mirror repository, readable by the operator alone. ADR 0028 and the runbook state the limit and name `serve mirror --rebuild` as the third step, so the erasure path is stated. Carried.

Upheld as advisory (Q1, hardening). `lowerContract` accepts 0 or a negative integer from a hostile server; the outcome fails closed (the next request is refused 409 and the server is stopped as `contract`), so a floor of 1 would only tighten the input check. Carried.

Upheld as advisory (Q10). The browser logs 'Failed to load resource … 409' once per capture of the created, exists and removed states (review/ui/console-projects-created.json, console-projects-exists.json, console-projects-removed.json and the per-capture files), the status spec.md:219 pins for those refusals; the dock shows the body's sentence, so no raw error reaches the person. Lowered to advisory in round 2 and unchanged since. On the reviewer's partial reading: the rubric rules the gate on the evidence the run produced, and the judge read the manifest (review/ui/manifest.json) itself: 23 declared states (20 on /projects, 3 on /settings#servers), each captured at the plan's three viewports (1280, 768, 360) in both schemes with its console file beside it, 138 captures in all; no state missing; motion none, so no interaction of a thesis is owed a row; every state the spec's capture line (spec.md:229) names is declared and captured. The judge also read the default-state capture the reviewer did not re-read (review/ui/projects-unnamed@1280-dark.png): the field prefilled `wizardingcode`, the New sentence, the levels enabled, as spec.md:206 says. The reviewer's volume is not a verdict; the console half of Q10 was read across every console file by grep, and nothing in the evidence raises a defect.

Upheld as advisory (Q5, a longer sentence). After 'Create and share' the dialog becomes 'Join a shared name?' without saying the create was refused because a teammate created the name meanwhile (review/ui/projects-exists@1280-dark.png). The spec's wording (journey 3) is met. Carried from round 3.

Upheld as advisory (Q5/Q11, cosmetic). The New, Joins, taken, removed and created sentences and both confirmation questions show the slug in literal Markdown backticks, while the bound sentence uses `<code class="wz-mono">` (review/ui/projects-new@1280-dark.png, projects-exists@1280-dark.png against projects-named@360-dark.png; the judge saw the backticks in projects-unnamed@1280-dark.png too). Readable, inconsistent. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q5). 'Set the level again' does not name the path that works, Nothing first and then a level (review/ui/projects-created@360-dark.png). The wording is the spec's. Carried.

Upheld as advisory (Q7/Q11, reads in context). In the dark scheme the disabled Shared name field looks like the enabled one; the warn sentence and the dimmed radios carry the held state (review/ui/projects-held@1280-dark.png). The reviewer did not re-read this capture in round 4; it is in this round's evidence set, taken after the route change, and the dock code it shows is unchanged since round 3, so the round-3 reading stands at the same severity.

Upheld as advisory (Q7, crowding that holds). At 360px each name line wraps into two or three lines, the counts line starts with '·' and '0' is split from 'members' (review/ui/settings-names@360-dark.png). No overflow, no hidden control. Carried.

Upheld as advisory (a change beyond the stated intent that reads clearly). Once bound, a 'Shared as' sentence stands where spec.md:208 describes a read-only field (review/ui/projects-named@360-dark.png). Carried.

Upheld as advisory (Q2, variants of captured templates). The reserved-file-name refusal (line 206) and the post-confirm 'Not changed' toast (line 361) reuse the captured refused and not-changed templates with strings no capture shows; the templates themselves are captured (review/ui/projects-refused@1280-dark.png, projects-not-changed@1280-dark.png). Carried.

Upheld as advisory (Q2, a rollback that exists). The ADR's summary goes from 'the names created since are lost' to 'a project bound to a lost name is `missing`' and leaves out the 'names held (server at contract 1)' state that lasts while the 0.7.0 image runs; the runbook (line 81) states it. The rollback is stated; one of its intermediate states is missing from the ADR's one-paragraph summary. Carried from rounds 2 and 3.

Upheld as advisory (Q1/Q4). A push answered `name` sets `missing` and the sweep retries at every later sweep with no backoff until the person sets the level again; the failure is visible as `missing` in `status`, `doctor` and the dock, so it is not a failure nobody would see. Carried.

Upheld as advisory (Q3). `serve purge name <alias> --yes` has no dry run and no undo; the write is limited to one named alias, is operator-only and needs `--yes`, and the runbook names the mirror and `serve mirror --rebuild`. Carried.

Upheld as advisory (Q1). A Receive-only teammate never pushes after a restore older than a name, so `missing` is never set on their side and their received copies under the name are dropped by the snapshot with no word on their machine. Carried.

Upheld as advisory. The spec's line states the client rollback (a 0.7.0 binary refuses the version 8 store; restore the upgrade's copy) and names where its sentence goes (the ADR and the release notes); the ADR and the runbook carry it, README.md does not, and the release item owes the notes line. The rollback is stated and the dependency named, so this is not an unstated rollback or dependency on a spec line, which would be a defect. Carried. Round 3's runbook finding (line 81) is resolved: `share names` is asked for 'while the server still answers', before `docker compose stop server`, and the first `cp` keeps `team-before-rollback.db` aside with its reason stated.

Upheld as advisory (Q5/Q6, no drift). The viewer's PUT now runs `prepareBinding` then `commitBinding` with or without `as`, the two-phase rule of the CLI (src/cli/commands/share.ts:265-291), spec.md:219 and ADR 0028; the round-3 drift is closed. The one difference, no `remoteAlias` passed, is the optional field of `binding.ts` the viewer has no working directory for.

Upheld as advisory (Q3/Q5). The 200 answer always carries the four keys spec.md:219 names (`level`, `old`, `boundAlias`, `sharedName`) and, after a server step, adds `named`, `created` and `joined`. The judge checked the consumers: the viewer's type (ui/src/api.ts:405) names the four keys, the dock reads `named` only on a refusal (ProjectsView.vue:350, as spec.md:219 says), and nothing but tests/integration/ui-sharing.test.ts reads `created` or `joined` on a 200. The three keys are additive, read by no other code or system, and beyond what the Design names on the 200: scope named as such, not a contract another piece relies on changed without its file. The viewer's type could name them as optional.

Upheld as advisory (Q2). The reviewer wrote `src/report.ts` and corrected it in parentheses; the line is src/sharing/report.ts:681. `importedStayCounts` filters `memories` on `status = 'active' AND origin = 'imported'` with no index on `origin`, so each `wouldLeave` call reads the table; the result is correct and no hook reads it. Carried.

Upheld as advisory (Q2). `nameItemOf` runs `nameCountsOf` (two queries) and `memberById` per row, so a `GET /v1/names` page may make up to 3×200 indexed reads; ADR 0028 records the choice and the page is capped. Carried.

Upheld as advisory (Q2). `receivedNameCounts` filters `knowledge_received` on `remote_alias` with no index, so each bound name reads that server's received entries twice on every `status`, `doctor` and Servers read; none of these is a hook path. Carried.
